title: `/api/v1/ai/*` answers 503 "AI service routes not yet initialized" forever when the AI route table is deliberately suppressed (unlicensed EE), and the Console requests `/ai/agents` on every page
body:
## Edition

ObjectOS Enterprise (licensed, self-managed), run with **no licence** (Community).

## Version

EE image 4.3.1 (`sha256:679eb7525e1ab3bfc732fc46433543ab388ba0cabc3157616e6bd2350210f658`, framework pin `63b86b38`). The same exit is on `main`: `packages/runtime/src/domains/ai.ts`, the `if (!routes)` branch.

## What happened / What you expected

On an unlicensed EE install, every Console page (all 42 Setup pages, Home, the Studio-built app) sends `GET /api/v1/ai/agents` and gets:

```
503 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE","message":"AI service routes not yet initialized","httpStatus":503}}
```

Each page then logs `Failed to load resource: … 503 (Service Unavailable)` to the browser console. Nothing renders wrong, but:

- the answer says the AI is *starting up* when it is in fact *off for this edition*. A 503 tells clients and operators to retry, and it never resolves;
- an operator debugging anything else sees a 503 on every page and goes looking for a broken AI service.

Expected: when AI is unavailable by design, `/ai/*` gives the same answer as the "unserveable" exit above it (capability unavailable, not a transient 503), and the Console stops requesting `/ai/agents` once it knows AI is unavailable, or treats that answer as "AI off" without an error.

## Cause

cloud#1514 made the unlicensed EE image suppress `registerRoutes`, so the AI service never publishes `__aiRoutes` (cloud `apps/objectos-ee/test/unlicensed-ai-routes-suppressed.test.ts`). `http-dispatcher`'s `getRegisteredAiRoutes()` then returns `undefined`, and the AI domain treats that as the boot-race window:

```ts
if (!routes) {
    if (denyAnonymous) return anonymousRefusal();
    return { handled: true, response: deps.error('AI service routes not yet initialized', 503) };
}
```

"Not published yet" and "deliberately not published" share one exit. The cloud test notes that the framework tree is read-only from the cloud side, and that a dispatcher change is filed here as the twin.

## Steps

1. Run `deploy/install.sh --image <4.3.1 digest> --url http://localhost --admin-email …` with no `--license-file`.
2. Sign in and open any Console page with DevTools open.
3. Every page shows `GET /api/v1/ai/agents` → 503 with the message above.

## Impact

Low. Nothing breaks, but there is a console error on every page of every unlicensed EE install, and its wording is misleading. Found during the clean-host install run for objectstack-ai/cloud#3582.
